title: Topics by Hand: Publish, Subscribe and the Order Things Happen In

questions.question: What problem does a topic solve?
options: The publisher and subscriber need to know a name and not each other, so a part can be replaced or a second consumer added without changing the first
questions.explanation: Every new part otherwise changes every old one.

questions.question: A message is published to a topic with no subscribers. What should happen?
options: It is dropped and counted: two such messages gave a dropped count of 2, and a subscriber who came later heard only 1 of 3
It is delivered to every topic
questions.explanation: A publisher cannot know who is listening.

questions.question: A handler unsubscribes a later subscriber during delivery. What does the bus do?
options: Skips it: the tokens are copied when the message goes out and each is checked before its call, so b was not called and the first message reached 2 subscribers
questions.explanation: Erasing from a list being walked skips or overruns.

questions.question: A handler publishes a message while handling one. When is it delivered?
options: After every subscriber of the first message has been called: the publish returned 0 and the log showed second heard 7 before out heard 7
questions.explanation: A queue keeps the order sensible.

questions.question: Why does the queue stop a ping and a pong that answer each other from overflowing the stack?
options: It turns the recursion into a loop: 5000 each ran with no nesting
questions.explanation: It is still a loop with no end if nothing stops it.

questions.question: What does this bus not do yet?
options: It is one thread with a string payload and no loss or delay: threads, typed payloads and a network are the later lessons
questions.explanation: Each of those is a question every middleware has to answer.
